statement: A large 4 by 4 by 4 cube is built from 64 unit cubes. How many different 2 by 2 by 2 cubes, each made of 8 of the unit cubes, can be found inside it? They are allowed to overlap.

choices.misconception: I cut the big cube into separate 2 by 2 by 2 blocks that do not overlap and counted only those.
I thought the small cube could start at any of 4 positions in each direction, $4 \times 4 \times 4$, but from the last position it would stick out.
I found 3 positions in each direction but added them, 3 + 3 + 3, instead of multiplying.
I found the 9 positions in one layer and multiplied by 4 layers, but there are only 3 positions going up as well.

hints: Slide a block 2 units long along an edge 4 units long. How many stops?
A 2 by 2 by 2 cube is fixed by where its corner nearest you sits. Count the possible positions in each of the three directions and multiply, because the directions are independent.
Along an edge of 4 units, a block 2 units long can start at 3 places.

solutions.reliable: In one direction, a block of length 2 inside a length of 4 can start at position 1, 2 or 3, so there are 4 - 2 + 1 = 3 places. The same is true across and up. Each choice of the three starting positions gives a different 2 by 2 by 2 cube, so there are $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$. The transferable idea: count overlapping blocks by sliding, with $n - k + 1$ positions in each direction.
solutions.elegant: Each 2 by 2 by 2 cube has a centre point where 8 of its unit cubes meet, and that point is a corner of the unit grid strictly inside the big cube. Those inside grid corners form a 3 by 3 by 3 array, so there are 27 such cubes.

whyOnTest: Tests the sliding-window count in three dimensions, where the classic slip is cutting the cube into separate pieces.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
